reader.decision: Approve the async taskq job with an emailed signed link as the primary fix. Streaming stays as the alternative and is not chosen now. I'm not raising idle_timeout_seconds.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the root cause is a long synchronous build in a web worker. Only the async job removes it and stops month-end worker starvation. Streaming still holds a worker and hits the 300s limit above about 2.3M rows. Nothing in the message says accountants need the file in the same click.

reconstruction.problem: export_invoices builds the whole CSV (1,840,211 rows) in one in-memory StringIO before sending any byte. The query takes 18s and the build takes 222s. gw-billing closes the connection after 30s with no bytes and returns 504 (gw-idle-timeout) to large tenants.
reconstruction.what_breaks: The accountant gets no file. The worker ignores the closed connection and keeps building until about second 240. At month end all 12 gunicorn workers are busy and /invoices p99 rises to 9.4s against 0.4s on a quiet day, so other tenants slow down.
reconstruction.fix: export_invoices in app/exports.py only enqueues a render_invoice_csv taskq job on the documents queue and returns 202. The new job in jobs/invoice_csv.py runs the query, writes the CSV in chunks to a temp file, calls storage.put and storage.signed_url, and emails the link with mailer.send, as jobs/invoice_pdf.py does.
reconstruction.cost: The contract changes: callers get an email instead of a file. About 900 month-end exports share the documents queue with PDFs, so a PDF can wait behind a large export. Queue concurrency was not found, so this is unchecked.

follow_up_questions: What is the documents queue concurrency, and can large CSV exports go on their own queue so PDFs don't wait behind them?
Do any API clients or scripts call GET /exports/invoices.csv and expect a CSV body, so the 202 contract would break them?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve the async taskq job with an emailed link. The message gives no sign that accountants need the file in the same click. Before shipping, check the documents queue concurrency, and consider a separate queue for exports so PDFs don't wait behind them.
